whatItIs: Alpha Brain is Onnit's flagship nootropic product, first released in 2011 and popularised through Joe Rogan's podcast endorsements. Alpha Brain has a published randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the finished product (Solomon 2016, PubMed 26876224): 63 adults aged 18–35, 6 weeks, improved delayed verbal recall and executive functioning; one author worked for Onnit Labs. howItWorks: Each Thesis formula targets a different goal, and Thesis lists an amount for every ingredient. Clarity: CDP choline 250mg, Panax ginseng 200mg, Lion's Mane 500mg, 7,8-dihydroxyflavone 30mg and vitamin B6 5mg. whatItIs: Nootropics Depot Lion's Mane Extract is a single-ingredient supplement providing standardised Hericium erinaceus fruiting body extract at 500mg per capsule. Nootropics Depot operates an ISO-certified in-house testing laboratory and publishes a Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for each batch. It enters the region as a personal-use supplement -- the same import pathway as the other imported products in this review -- and we have not verified a local product registration with the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) in Malaysia, the Thai FDA, FDA Philippines, the Badan Pengawas Obat dan Makanan (BPOM) in Indonesia or the Vietnam Food Administration (VFA).
howItWorks: Lion's Mane extracts raised Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) in cell and mouse studies, but in one cell study the fruiting body's hericenones did not (Mori 2008); the compound shown to reach the brain, erinacine A, comes from the mycelium and was tested in rats (Tsai 2021). No human trial has measured NGF. NGF promotes neuronal survival, axon growth, and maintenance of neurons in the hippocampus and cortex -- the regions responsible for learning and memory. Nootropics Depot uses a standardised fruiting body extract rather than mycelium.
whatToExpect: Lion's Mane is a long-game supplement. Pilot trials reported small acute effects within 1–2 hours. In a trial in adults with mild cognitive impairment, scores improved after 16 weeks of 3g a day and fell again within 4 weeks of stopping (Mori 2009). At the label's 1–2 capsules a day (500–1,000mg), this product reaches at most the low end of the pilot-trial doses (1–1.8g) and a third of the 3g a day used by Mori 2009. For best results, take consistently every day. This product is best combined with a multi-ingredient stack (e.g. Mind Lab Pro already contains Lion's Mane) rather than used as a standalone primary supplement.

whatItIs: Blackmores is an Australian health company founded in 1932. Brain Active contained one active ingredient: Longvida® turmeric extract (Curcuma longa dry concentrate), 400mg per capsule, equivalent to 5.4g dry rhizome and 80mg curcumin. Blackmores Singapore sold it in packs of 30 capsules at an RSP of S$51 (product page archived 2022-05-23). The product has been discontinued: Blackmores Singapore's brain-health category and Guardian Singapore's brain shelf no longer carry it (checked 2026-09-28).
howItWorks: Curcumin is the main active compound in turmeric. Longvida is a solid lipid curcumin formulation that Blackmores Singapore described as an enhanced bioavailable form of curcumin. Two placebo-controlled trials by the same research group tested 400mg Longvida daily (80mg curcumin) in healthy older adults: Cox et al. 2015 (J Psychopharmacol; 60 adults aged 60-85) found better sustained attention and working memory one hour after a dose, and better working memory and less fatigue after 4 weeks; Cox et al. 2020 (Nutrients; 80 adults aged 50-80) found better working memory at 12 weeks and lower fatigue scores at 4 and 12 weeks. The 2020 trial was funded by Verdure Sciences, which makes Longvida.
whatToExpect: Based on the two Longvida trials: possible effects on working memory and fatigue over 4 to 12 weeks of daily use, plus attention and working-memory effects one hour after a dose in the 2015 trial. Both trials studied healthy adults aged 50 to 85; neither tested younger adults. In the 2020 trial, blood glucose was higher in the curcumin group than with placebo. The product is discontinued, so this describes what the formula offered, not a product you can buy.

whatItIs: Memo Plus Gold is a Philippine food supplement containing a single active ingredient: 125mg of Bacopa Monnieri extract per capsule. It is stocked by major pharmacy chains (Mercury Drug, Watsons, Southstar) and online marketplaces, and is registered with the Philippine Food and Drug Administration (FDA Philippines). Unlike the multi-ingredient imported stacks elsewhere in this review, it is a focused, traditional single-herb product. Malaysia's National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) register lists 'Memo Plus Gold Capsule 125 mg' as MAL05092320T, held by OZE Marketing Sdn. Bhd. (QUEST3+ search, checked 2026-10-06). howItWorks: Bacopa Monnieri is a botanical with trial evidence for memory free recall (Pase 2012). Its proposed effects on the acetylcholine and serotonin systems come from animal and laboratory studies. The label dose of two 125mg capsules daily (250mg/day) is below the 300–450mg/day range of the trials in the systematic review we cite (Pase 2012). Because bacosides are fat-soluble, taking the capsules with a meal containing some fat is the standard advice.
whatToExpect: Bacopa is a slow-build, cumulative supplement — not an acute focus pill. Most of its measured benefits to memory and recall appear after 8-12 weeks of consistent daily use, so regularity matters far more than any single dose. A minority of users notice mild digestive upset in the first few weeks; this typically resolves. A 30-capsule bottle lasts about 15 days at the label dose, so plan on roughly two bottles per month. Taking it with a meal containing some fat is the standard advice.

summary: A zero-sugar nootropic energy drink in a can from UK brand Neutonic. Each 330ml can gives 120mg natural caffeine, 500mg citicoline (as Cognizin®), 400mg L-theanine, 400mg rhodiola extract and 200mg Panax ginseng extract, plus eight B vitamins. Caffeine, citicoline and L-theanine meet our reference doses; the rhodiola extract states no standardisation, and we have no reference dose on file for ginseng. With Singapore or Malaysia selected, neutonic.com sells a 12-can pack for £29.99 one-time, in pounds sterling (checked 2026-10-19); its product page says 'Worldwide shipping available'.
whatItIs: Neutonic Productivity Drink is a carbonated, ready-to-drink can from Neutonic, a UK brand whose range also includes caffeine-free Brain Capsules. One can is one serving ('Each can contains one serving'), and the vendor's recommended serving is one can a day. With Singapore or Malaysia selected, neutonic.com sells it in packs of 12 cans in one flavour (White Peach, Tropical Ice, Strawberry Lemonade, Wild Citrus, Blue Raspberry or Orange Sunrise) or as a mixed-flavour pack. Besides the actives, the ingredient list names carbonated water, the acidity regulators citric acid and trisodium citrate, natural flavourings, the sweeteners sucralose and acesulfame K, and potassium sorbate as a preservative; the vitamin blend lists niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, riboflavin, thiamine, folic acid (as L-methylfolate), biotin and vitamin B12 (as methylcobalamin), which the vendor's panel gives as 100% of the reference intake (RI). The vendor says the drink is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.
howItWorks: Caffeine (120mg) blocks adenosine receptors; at low-to-moderate doses it consistently improves alertness, vigilance, attention and reaction time, with less consistent effects on memory (McLellan 2016, a narrative review). L-theanine (400mg, twice the top of our 100-200mg reference range) is an amino acid from green tea: in an 11-study meta-analysis, caffeine plus L-theanine had moderate effects versus placebo on alertness and attention-switching accuracy (Camfield 2014), but Foxe 2012 found no added benefit over either compound alone, and in a controlled trial (Rogers 2008, PubMed 17891480) L-theanine did not significantly reduce caffeine jitteriness. Citicoline (500mg, as Cognizin®) is a precursor to acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine; its memory evidence comes from older adults with inefficient memory at 1,000-2,000mg a day (Spiers 1996), and a Cochrane review found no evidence of an attention benefit in older adults with chronic cerebral disorders. Rhodiola is an adaptogen: small trials of the SHR-5 extract found less mental fatigue, but a 2012 systematic review rated every included study at high or unclear risk of bias, and the product page does not say which extract or standardisation is used. We have no reference dose on file for Panax ginseng. Neutonic Productivity Drink itself has not been tested in a published trial; the vendor's claims rest on ingredient-level research.
whatToExpect: Caffeine's alerting effect typically starts within 15-45 minutes, the onset on our caffeine page; the vendor suggests a can before 'any high demand session', from a morning start to training. Each can has 120mg caffeine and the vendor recommends one can a day, advising drinkers to be mindful of their total caffeine intake, so count it toward your daily total if you also drink coffee. Citicoline's memory effects in trials were measured after 2-3 months, so a single can should not be expected to change memory. With Singapore selected, neutonic.com prices a 12-can pack at £29.99 one-time or £25.50 a delivery on a subscription (Subscribe & Save 15%), checked 2026-10-19. The product page says 'Worldwide shipping available'; the shipping page has no Singapore or Malaysia section and says 'When ordering internationally you may have to pay import duty depending on what you’ve ordered and its declared value' (neutonic.com/pages/shipping-returns, checked 2026-10-19).

whatItIs: Neutonic Brain Capsules (UK edition) are the caffeine-free capsules Neutonic sells on its main store, which serves Singapore and Malaysia in pounds sterling. They carry the UK label rather than the US one: the actives and amounts are the same as on the US bottle, but this label prints no bacoside standardisation for the bacopa extract (the US label states 55% bacosides), its ingredient list names 'Panax Ginseng Root' where its dose panel says '200mg Panax Ginseng Extract', and the capsule shell is rice hull concentrate and hypromellose coloured with iron oxide and titanium dioxide. A bottle holds 90 capsules, 30 daily servings of 3; the vendor says the capsules can be taken together or spread through the day. The vitamin blend lists niacin, pantothenic acid, biotin, vitamin B6, thiamin, riboflavin, folic acid (as calcium 5-methyltetrahydrofolate) and vitamin B12 (as cyanocobalamin), which the vendor's panel gives as 100% of the reference intake (RI). howItWorks: Citicoline (500mg, as Cognizin®) is a precursor to acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine; its memory evidence comes from older adults with inefficient memory at 1,000-2,000mg a day (Spiers 1996), and a Cochrane review found no evidence of an attention benefit in older adults with chronic cerebral disorders. Bacopa (300mg) has the most memory evidence here: two 12-week trials in healthy older adults improved delayed word recall at 300mg a day (Calabrese 2008; Morgan & Stevens 2010), though the newest 12-week trial at that dose (Lopresti 2025) found no effect on verbal learning, attention or working memory. Our reference dose is for an extract with at least 50% bacosides, and this label does not print the bacoside content. The positive ginkgo trials were in dementia, mainly at 240mg a day of the EGb 761 extract for 22-26 weeks (Tan 2015 meta-analysis); this product has 120mg with no standardisation on the product page, and the GEM trial found no preventive effect on dementia in people aged 75 and over. Rhodiola is an adaptogen: small trials of the SHR-5 extract found less mental fatigue, but a 2012 systematic review rated every included study at high or unclear risk of bias, and the product page does not say which extract or standardisation is used. We have no reference dose on file for Panax ginseng. Brain Capsules themselves have not been tested in a published trial; the vendor's claims rest on ingredient-level research.
whatToExpect: Brain Capsules are built for daily use rather than a quick effect: the vendor recommends taking them every day for at least 30 days to experience the full benefits, and the positive bacopa memory trials ran for 12 weeks. There is no caffeine, so the timing is flexible, and the vendor says they can be taken alongside its caffeinated drink. Take 3 capsules a day. Our bacopa page notes digestive effects (increased stool frequency, abdominal cramps, nausea) at 300mg a day in a 12-week trial in older adults, so taking the capsules with food may help.
